classification.difficultyReason: Convert a compass bearing and use parallel north references to find the reverse true bearing.

content.prompt: The compass bearing of $B$ from $A$ is $\mathrm{N}38^{\circ}\mathrm{E}$. What is the true bearing of $A$ from $B$?

spec.description: Compass axes at A, B northeast of A, a dashed perpendicular from B to the eastward axis, its right-angle marker, and the not-to-scale notice.
spec.mathematics: AB has bearing 038 degrees from A. B is placed using offset (3 sin 38 degrees, 3 cos 38 degrees); the coordinate length is a drawing parameter, not a numerical given.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied 38-degree angle is visible; the reverse bearing is answer content.

answer.worked:
The north references are parallel. The smaller angle at $B$ is
$$\begin{aligned}\theta &= 180^{\circ}-38^{\circ}\\\theta &= 142^{\circ}.\end{aligned}$$
Cointerior angles sum to $180^{\circ}$. The clockwise bearing of $A$ from $B$ is
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Bearing} &= 360^{\circ}-142^{\circ}\\\text{Bearing} &= 218^{\circ}.\end{aligned}$$
